evidence_items.publisher: Science; abstract reproduced by Stanford SCALE
evidence_items.explanation: The randomized experiment involved 453 professionals completing occupation-specific writing assignments. Substantial savings on completed work, accompanied by higher assessed quality, contradict the blanket claim under the stated reading of business copy.

evidence_items.publisher: Shakked Noy and Whitney Zhang, MIT
evidence_items.explanation: The original study measured complete assignments and examined editing after generated text was inserted. It reports limited editing and no detected quality advantage from that editing, directly addressing the proposed mechanism that revision consumes the savings.

evidence_items.locator: Section Simulating work for chatbots, discussion of study limitations
evidence_items.explanation: The institutional account says the assignments did not require company-specific context or precise factual accuracy, and factual accuracy was not independently checked. Additional production requirements could reduce the measured savings.

unresolved_gaps: The experiment does not measure all downstream fact-checking, brand review, or client approval needed for publication.
